title: You Can't Unring the Bell
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece warns that leaders live one careless remark away from serious reputational damage, and that no apology can fully undo an offensive statement once it is public. It links this vulnerability to ego, arguing that leaders who feel untouchable are the ones most likely to say something that lands badly, whether through genuine offense or a joke that misfires. The article frames leadership visibility as a double-edged sword: it doesn't require playing it safe, but it does require constant awareness that words will always be read as a reflection of character. It closes with a blunt reminder to check ego before stepping into any leadership moment.
points: Argues leaders are permanently one remark away from serious career damage
Links offensive missteps to unchecked ego and a false sense of invulnerability
Notes humor and jokes are a common, underestimated source of leadership missteps
Closes with a call to check ego before any high-visibility leadership moment
quotes: Leaders are held to an even higher standard. Once a leader says, does, or writes something decidedly offensive, the career curtains come crashing down.
It is worth committing to memory that every leader, no matter how important, is only one utterance away from ending their career.
Once the insensitive remark or action is shared, no one can unring the bell.
When leaders operate largely from ego, thinking they are infallible in the moment, they can say the craziest things.
Leaders don’t attempt extreme humor unless they are hugely comfortable with themselves and think they are above being misinterpreted.
So before you take any leadership stage, please check your ego at the door.
